messages:
Eli: quick follow-up from today's all-hands ": thanks for the questions earlier. posting a live thread for any leftover strategy/positioning asks.
Maya: short framing ": our mission stays: make inference predictable and cheap enough for devs to build on it. not just fastest model, but predictable unit economics.
Sofia: question ": do we have prioritized verticals (e.g., search, contact centers, analytics) or stay horizontal?
Jordan: we stay horizontal but will kick off 2 focused GTM plays: platform teams at scale-ups, and compliance-heavy industries (health/finance). those get runway and templates.
Ravi: competitor question ": big clouds bundle model + infra. do we partner with them or compete on infra?
Maya: pragmatic approach ": integrate where customers want (marketplace listings), but compete on controls/observability and cost. think: "if you need strict latency and rollbacks, pick us."
Ben: product ask ": what are the must-have console features this quarter?
Liz: must-haves: per-route token cost, rollout UI for canary/A-B, private deploy health checks, and a short onboarding checklist for Dedicated.
Sofia: sales angle ": how do we talk about "serving-first" without sounding like we don't care about model quality?
Eli: frame it as "we maximize the value of your chosen model" — we make quality repeatable at scale. that resonates with engineering buyers.
Jordan: tactical: include a one-pager that maps "model choice" -> "serving knobs" so PMs understand tradeoffs.
Ravi: ops question ": any change to incident response SLAs for Dedicated vs Hosted?
Maya: Dedicated will get a tightened SLA next year and a documented escalation path. Hosted keeps the standard uptime guarantees.
Ben: engineering ask ": can we get a public benchmarking artifact we can cite?
Liz: yes — marketing+eng will publish a reproducible benchmark with notebooks and configs.
AllHandsBot: poll: "Which message should be prioritized in external comms?" options: 1) predictability 2) unit economics 3) multi-deploy flexibility 4) observability. react 1/2/3/4.
Sofia: follow-up: open-source involvement? customers ask about auditability and community models.
Maya: we will continue contributing infra optimizations and some tooling; not training big models. OSS helps validate our approach.
Eli: FYI for folks: expect a 2-page FAQ + slide deck for sales by next Tue.
Ben: noted — will add benchmark links and a short demo script.
Jordan: also adding a "why not cloud endpoint" slide with concrete scenarios (fallbacks, cost spikes, private deployments).
Ravi: I'll draft the Dedicated runbook checklist customers asked for.
Liz: I'll coordinate the benchmark repo and assign eng owners.
Eli: thanks team. keep sending short threads here if anything pops up. we'll consolidate into an FAQ and share a recording. :clap:
